Entry.EnglishText: Old Man

Entry.EnglishText: Millionaire

Entry.JapaneseText: <Kyle>
Entry.EnglishText: Kyle

Entry.JapaneseText: クレスタの街・宿屋
Entry.EnglishText: Cresta City - Inn

Entry.JapaneseText: クレスタ
Entry.EnglishText: Cresta

Entry.JapaneseText: 孤児院の子をひきとろうと思って この街にきたんじゃが どの子にするかなんて選べないねえ････
Entry.EnglishText: I came to this city to adopt a child from the orphanage,but I can't choose which child to take in.

Entry.JapaneseText: 兄弟みたいに仲のいい あの子たちを引きはなすなんて なんだか、しのびなくて････
Entry.EnglishText: I can't bear to part with them, they're like brothers to me.

Entry.JapaneseText: いっそのこと ワシたちがこの街に 引っこしてこようかねぇ
Entry.EnglishText: Maybe we should just move to this town.

Entry.JapaneseText: ここは平和で静かで良いところじゃよ この幸せが永遠に続いたらいいのにのぉ
Entry.EnglishText: It's nice and peaceful and quiet here. I wish this happiness could last forever.

Entry.JapaneseText: この歳になると 子供の笑顔が恋しくてね 孤児を引き取りたいって申し出たんだ
Entry.EnglishText: At my age, I miss the smile of a child, so I offered to adopt an orphan.

Entry.JapaneseText: だけど、ルーティさんに断られたよ 「ご厚意はありがたいのですが みんな、ウチの子ですから」ってね
Entry.EnglishText: But Ms. Rutee refused, saying, "We appreciate your kindness, but they're all our children.

Entry.JapaneseText: あの子たちは 孤児院で生活するのが いちばん幸せなのかもしれないね
Entry.EnglishText: Maybe those kids are happiest living in an orphanage.

Entry.JapaneseText: あの、お日さまのような 笑顔を見ていると そんな気がしてくるよ
Entry.EnglishText: I feel that way when I look at that sunny smile.

Entry.JapaneseText: 孤児院の子供たちが どうして、あんなに笑えるのかを ずっと考えていたのじゃよ
Entry.EnglishText: I've been trying to figure out why the kids at the orphanage can smile so much.

Entry.JapaneseText: だけど、ようやくわかったわい なんのことはない スタンさんとルーティさんを 親として、あそこは家族なんじゃとな
Entry.EnglishText: But I finally understood that Stahn and Rutee were my parents, and that we were a family.

Entry.JapaneseText: 孤児院は経営が苦しそうだから 子供を引き取ろうと考えておったが そんな必要はなかったみたいじゃな
Entry.EnglishText: The orphanage was struggling, so I thought I'd take the kids in, but it looks like that wasn't necessary.

Entry.JapaneseText: 私の娘が、この街に 嫁いだんですけどね････
Entry.EnglishText: My daughter married into this city...

Entry.JapaneseText: まさか、こんな田舎だったなんて なぜアイグレッテでの裕福な生活を捨てて ここへ来たのでしょう？
Entry.EnglishText: I had no idea it was this rural. Why did I leave my wealthy life in Aigrette to come here?

Entry.JapaneseText: 住みやすい街なら、他にいくらでも あるでしょうに････
Entry.EnglishText: I'm sure there are plenty of other cities that are more habitable.

Entry.JapaneseText: なんだか、土クサイですし････ 洗練されたワタクシには 似合わない場所ですねえ
Entry.EnglishText: This place smells like shit, not really a place for someone sophisticated like me...

Entry.JapaneseText: ハァ････ 娘はアイグレッテに戻る気は 無いようね
Entry.EnglishText: Huh...my daughter doesn't seem to want to go back to Aiglette.

Entry.JapaneseText: 住みなれてしまえば、ここも 良い場所には違いないんだけど アイグレッテ以上ではないわ
Entry.EnglishText: It must be a nice place to live once you get used to it, but it's not better than Aigrette.

Entry.JapaneseText: 何と言ってもアイグレッテには エルレイン様がいらっしゃるんですもの
Entry.EnglishText: After all, Lady Elrane is in Aigrette.

Entry.JapaneseText: アイグレッテは エルレイン様の加護を受けた街
Entry.EnglishText: Aigrette is a city blessed by Lady Elrane.

Entry.JapaneseText: アイグレッテ以上の 街なんて無いのに････ There is no city better than Aiglette...
ここの食事は とても、おいしいですねぇ
Entry.EnglishText: The food here is very, very good!

Entry.JapaneseText: 田舎風の味つけも 苦になりませんし
Entry.EnglishText: I don't mind the country-style flavoring.

Entry.JapaneseText: ここの料理は、ウチの母さん直伝なんだよ 母さんも、誰かに 料理を教わったらしいけどね
Entry.EnglishText: The recipes here were handed down from my mother, who also learned how to cook from someone else.

Entry.JapaneseText: アナタのお母さまに 料理を教えたのは いったい、誰なのでしょう
Entry.EnglishText: Who taught your mother how to cook?

Entry.JapaneseText: ぜひ、ウチ専属のシェフに なってほしいですわ
Entry.EnglishText: I would love to have her as my personal chef.

Entry.JapaneseText: 風景画がある どこかの遺跡の絵のようだ
Entry.EnglishText: There's a landscape painting. Looks like a painting of some ruins.

Entry.JapaneseText: 緑に覆われた遺跡の絵だ クレスタの近くに、そんな場所があったような････
Entry.EnglishText: It's a picture of ruins covered in greenery. There was such a place near Cresta.

Entry.JapaneseText: ここは客室 勝手に触らないでおこう
Entry.EnglishText: This is a guest room. Let's not touch it without permission.

Entry.JapaneseText: 何も入っていないようだ
Entry.EnglishText: Doesn't look like there's anything in there.

Entry.JapaneseText: 奥に何かありそうですが････？
Entry.EnglishText: Is there something in the back...?

Entry.JapaneseText: 何かあるな････
Entry.EnglishText: There's something here...

Entry.JapaneseText: <item:00000122>を手に入れました
Entry.EnglishText: Acquired <item:00000122>.

Entry.JapaneseText: これは････ ネルソンさんの趣味かな････
Entry.EnglishText: This... I wonder if this is one of Nelson's hobbies...

Entry.JapaneseText: いってらっしゃいませ
Entry.EnglishText: Have a good day.
It'll be <0B:00000001>{14}{34}{08}{C0}<0B:00000000> gald a night. Would you like to stay?

Entry.JapaneseText: お泊まりになりますか？
Entry.EnglishText: Would you like to stay?

Entry.JapaneseText: ごゆっくりお休みください
Entry.EnglishText: Have a good night.

Entry.JapaneseText: おはようございます
Entry.EnglishText: Good morning.

Entry.JapaneseText: お金が足りません
Entry.EnglishText: Don't have enough money.

Entry.JapaneseText: またのおこしをお待ちしております
Entry.EnglishText: I look forward to seeing you again.
